title: Finite exceptional preservation and finite free coefficient comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $B$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Suppose $f$ admits a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary small-etale-site coefficients, compact support $Rf_{!,B}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and the bounded constructible categories [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The bounded-below etale right adjoint $f_B^!$ exists, and both $Rf_{!,B}$ and $f_B^!$ preserve bounded constructibility, so their adjunction restricts to these full subcategories.

For a finite extension $B\subset C$ of finite fields, put $T_W=C_W\otimes^L_{B_W}-$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The finite-free compact-support comparison $c:T_YRf_{!,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,C}T_X$ and the counit-defined exceptional comparison
$$T_Xf_B^!L\xrightarrow{\sim}f_C^!T_YL\qquad(L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B))$$
are natural isomorphisms. The latter is the adjoint of
$$Rf_{!,C}T_Xf_B^!L\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}T_YRf_{!,B}f_B^!L\xrightarrow{T_Y\epsilon_L}T_YL.$$
Here $\epsilon$ is the exceptional counit; thus this comparison is fixed by adjunction, including its normalization.

source.place: Section 6.7 and Lemma 6.7.18, with complete local ring R=B and maximal ideal zero; compact-support finiteness by compactification and Theorem 6.7.1; finite-free coefficient version of the adjunction comparison in the proof of Lemma 6.7.18

proof.text: Fix a compactification $f=pj$. Its middle scheme is Noetherian, since $p$ is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $Y$. A finite-type morphism between Noetherian schemes is finitely presented: on affine charts this is exactly the finite-generation-of-relations assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], and quasi-separatedness follows from Noetherianity. Thus the proper case of [lem-per-quasi-excellent-etale-direct-image-finiteness] applies to $p$. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact. It preserves constructible sheaves: keep their finitely many locally closed strata in $X$ and add the closed complement in the middle scheme, where the sheaf is zero. Hence the compactification formula $Rf_{!,B}=Rp_{*,B}j_!$ sends bounded constructible complexes to bounded constructible complexes.

The ambient ordinary-etale adjoint $G_B=f_B^\times$ exists by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. We check its bounded-below restriction rather than assume one from a pro-etale construction. By Step 1 and [lem-per-quasi-excellent-etale-direct-image-finiteness], $R^qp_*M=0$ for all $q>d$ with a single $d$. Sheaves of constant-ring modules form a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Applying [lem-etale-derived-functor-upper-amplitude] to $p_*$ shows that $Rp_*$ sends $D^{\le b}$ into $D^{\le b+d}$ even on the unbounded categories. Exact $j_!$ has amplitude zero. Consequently [lem-etale-upper-shriek-bounded-below-from-amplitude] applies to $Rf_!$, and $G_B$ preserves $D^+$. Its restriction is the bounded-below right adjoint denoted $f_B^!$. The same reasoning applies to every finite coefficient field used below.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, existence assertion; bounded-below justification by finite cohomological dimension

proof.text: Exact inverse image preserves bounded constructibility. Indeed, pull back the finite stratification of each cohomology sheaf, then its local constant trivializations; their finite module values remain the same. This uses the actual stratification and constant-sheaf pullback assertions, not a definition of a different coefficient category. Also, for $N=\ell$, the finite etale Tate sheaf $B_T(a)$ is locally free of rank one for every integer $a$. Tensor with it is therefore exact and preserves the finite locally constant descriptions on each stratum. In particular $K\mapsto p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ preserves bounded constructibility for the projection $p_d:\mathbf A^d_T\to T$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, smooth-factor calculation; finite-etale Tate line as in Stacks Kummer theory

proof.text:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion with $P$ Noetherian excellent and $\ell$ invertible, and let $h:O\hookrightarrow P$ be its open complement. For bounded constructible $M$ on $P$, Step 3 puts $h^*M$ in $D^b_c(O,B)$. The morphism $h$ is finitely presented, since it is an open immersion into a Noetherian scheme; the nonproper case of [lem-per-quasi-excellent-etale-direct-image-finiteness] applies. Thus $Rh_*h^*M$ is bounded constructible. The actual counit/unit triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] is
$$i_*Ri^!M\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Rh_*h^*M\longrightarrow(i_*Ri^!M)[1].$$
Its cohomology exact sequence and the kernel, cokernel and extension closure of [thm-constructible-serre] show that $i_*Ri^!M$ is bounded constructible. Finally $i^*i_*\cong1$ on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-kun-04ca]; this natural counit respects every constant scalar and hence is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves and of their termwise complexes. Exact inverse image and Step 3 therefore give $Ri^!M=i^*(i_*Ri^!M)\in D^b_c(Z,B)$. This proves the closed step without requiring $i$ regular.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, closed-factor localization argument; ordinary direct-image finiteness Theorem 6.7.1

proof.text: Cover $X$ by finitely many affine opens $U$ mapping into affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$, with inclusions $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$. Such a finite cover exists by the finite-type definition and the finite affine cover of $Y$. The coordinate algebra of $U$ is finite type over $R$, so choosing finitely many algebra generators exhibits $U$ as a closed subscheme $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$. Thus $fu=vp_ni$. The polynomial coordinate ring of $\mathbf A^n_V$ is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; it is Noetherian, and $\ell$ stays invertible. All these maps admit compactifications: opens and closed immersions have their evident ones, and $\mathbf A^n_V$ is the standard open of $\mathbf P^n_V$. Thus every compact-support composition and adjoint below is in its stated domain.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, local closed-immersion/smooth factorization, made on affine charts

proof.text:
For $L\in D^b_c(Y,B)$ and a test object $H\in D^+(U,B)$, compact-support composition and the open adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,u^*f_B^!L)=\operatorname{Hom}(R(fu)_{!,B}H,L)
=\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{n!,B}i_*H,v^*L).$$
The last equality uses $fu=vp_ni$ and the open adjunction $v_!\dashv v^*$. The affine-space adjunction [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] applies with $A=B$ and $N=\ell$, over the Noetherian base $V$. Following it by the closed adjunction [lem-exc-closed-ambient] identifies the last Hom with
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,Ri^!(p_n^*v^*L(n)[2n])).$$
Both represented objects belong to $D^+$: the left one by Step 2, the right one by Steps 3 and 4. Yoneda on $D^+(U,B)$ gives $u^*f_B^!L\cong Ri^!(p_n^*v^*L(n)[2n])$. Steps 3 and 4 prove this object bounded constructible. This argument uses the ordinary etale affine-space adjunction over an arbitrary Noetherian base, not a purity statement restricted to a finite-field base.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, factorization into closed immersion and smooth projection; affine-space adjunction follows the lecture-notes route

proof.text: The cover in Step 5 is finite, so take the smallest lower and largest upper cohomological bounds for the objects in Step 6. Cohomology sheaves restrict by exact inverse image; outside this common interval they vanish on a cover and hence vanish. For each remaining degree, order the affine opens $U_1,\ldots,U_r$. Intersect each stratum on $U_j$ with $U_j\setminus\bigcup_{k<j}U_k$. These form a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes, with the same locally constant finite module descriptions. This is exactly bounded constructibility. If $X$ is empty the output is zero and no maximum is needed. Together with Step 1 this proves that both functors preserve $D^b_c$. Since these categories are full, the ambient Hom bijections, units and counits restrict to them.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, locality of the constructibility assertion; explicit finite-cover gluing

proof.text: Now let $B\subset C$ be a finite extension of finite fields. Write $U_W$ for restriction of scalars on $W=X,Y$, and $T_W=C_W\otimes^L_{B_W}-$. A $B$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $C$ identifies $U_WT_WK$ with $K^{\oplus r}$, naturally in $K$. Thus $T_W$ is exact, preserves bounded constructibility, and agrees with underived coefficient extension; $U_W$ is exact and reflects isomorphisms. The general coefficient adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] gives $T_W\dashv U_W$, including its unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. These functors restrict to $D^+$, since the finite free tensor is exact.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 06YY, scalar adjunction; finite-free specialization

proof.text:
For bounded-below $C$-complexes, the same compactification gives a natural identification
$$U_YRf_{!,C}\cong Rf_{!,B}U_X.$$
For $j_!$ the identification is the identity on the sheafified extension-by-zero construction: restriction of scalars changes no underlying abelian sheaf. For $Rp_*$ it is exactly [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], which states the derived comparison, not just the underived sectionwise identity. Their composite gives the displayed identification for $Rp_*j_!$. In particular it applies to all bounded constructible inputs.

Put $F_B=Rf_{!,B}$ and $F_C=Rf_{!,C}$. For $K\in D^+(X,B)$ let $\eta_K:K\to U_XT_XK$ be the unit of Step 8, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and let $g_K:F_BK\to U_YF_CT_XK$ be $F_B(\eta_K)$ followed by the identification $F_BU_XT_XK\cong U_YF_CT_XK$ of Step 9. Define $c_K:T_YF_BK\to F_CT_XK$ as the $T_Y\dashv U_Y$ transpose of $g_K$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. It is a morphism of $D^+(Y,C)$, natural in $K$ since $\eta$, $F_B$ and the Step 9 identification are natural, and it involves no basis. To compute it, let $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ be a $B$-basis of $C$ and $s_{e_a}=e_a\eta_K:K\to U_XT_XK$, $x\mapsto e_a\otimes x$. The $e_a$-summand inclusion of $F_BK$ into $U_YT_YF_BK$ is $e_a\eta_{F_BK}$. Because $c_K$ is $C$-linear, the triangle identity $U_Y(c_K)\eta_{F_BK}=g_K$ gives $U_Y(c_K)\,e_a\eta_{F_BK}=e_ag_K$. The Step 9 identification is natural for the $C$-endomorphism $e_a$ of $T_XK$, and $F_C$ sends multiplication by $e_a$ to multiplication by $e_a$; hence $e_ag_K$ is $F_B(s_{e_a})$ followed by Step 9. So the basis identifies the underlying map of $c_K$ with the canonical biproduct comparison $\bigoplus_{a=1}^rF_BK\to F_B(\bigoplus_{a=1}^rK)\cong F_BU_XT_XK$. It is an isomorphism because $Rp_*j_!$ is additive. Restriction reflects isomorphisms, hence $c$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, extension square; finite-free basis calculation of its map

proof.text:
Write $G_B=f_B^!$, $G_C=f_C^!$. For $H\in D^+(X,B)$ and $N\in D^+(Y,C)$, the adjunctions and $c$ give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(H,U_XG_CN)
=\operatorname{Hom}_C(T_XH,G_CN)
=\operatorname{Hom}_C(F_CT_XH,N)
=\operatorname{Hom}_C(T_YF_BH,N)
=\operatorname{Hom}_B(F_BH,U_YN)
=\operatorname{Hom}_B(H,G_BU_YN).$$
Here every coefficient extension remains bounded below by Step 8, and every compact support remains bounded below by its derived definition. Yoneda gives a natural isomorphism $b_N:U_XG_CN\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BU_YN$. The bijections fix this isomorphism and its normalization; no arbitrary identification of the exceptional adjoints is being made.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, comparison of corresponding adjoint squares; finite-free field-extension version

proof.text:
For $L\in D^b_c(Y,B)$ define $\alpha_L:T_XG_BL\to G_CT_YL$ to be the $F_C\dashv G_C$ transpose of $(T_Y\epsilon_L)c^{-1}_{G_BL}$, exactly as in the statement. Check its invertibility on underlying $B$-complexes. Under $b_{T_YL}$ from Step 11, the composite of $U_X\alpha_L$ with the $e_a$-summand inclusion $G_BL\to U_XT_XG_BL$ has $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose $s_{e_a}\epsilon_L$: this follows by substituting the defining transpose of $\alpha_L$ and cancelling $c^{-1}c$, whose $e_a$ component is $F_B(s_{e_a})$ by Step 10. By the adjunction identity it is therefore $G_B(s_{e_a})$. Consequently
$$b_{T_YL}\,U_X\alpha_L:\bigoplus_{a=1}^rG_BL\longrightarrow G_B(\bigoplus_{a=1}^rL)$$
is the canonical finite-biproduct comparison. It is an isomorphism: a right adjoint preserves finite products by its Hom bijections, and finite products equal finite coproducts in these additive categories. Thus $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism, since $b$ is and $U_X$ reflects isomorphisms. Its construction by transpose is natural in $L$ and retains exactly the exceptional counit specified in the statement. No separability trace, field cohomological-dimension bound, or change of sites is used.

Sources read: BS §6.7, Thm 6.7.1 and Lemmas 6.7.2/6.7.17/6.7.18/6.7.19 (pp.55, 57-58); ILO Introduction Thm 1 and Exposé XIII 1.1.1. Statement and coefficient category are unchanged, and there is no SGA. Batch 5: lem-etale-upper-shriek-bounded-below-from-amplitude and cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction are general ordinary-étale finite-coefficient six-functor results. Neither assumption gives them (both are stated for Q̄ℓ pro-étale coefficients over a field), and neither is a step of the TF or PD proofs. The flagged endpoints (lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects, lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar) are generic sheaf lemmas. Both nodes are already in both batch-5 closures without this delivery (via thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class and thm-sf-ctf-stability→lem-coef-finite-dualizing, and via the statement closure of nt-assume-poincare-duality), so there is no RETURN on that ground. Steps 1-9, 11 and 12 check: I recomputed the Step 6 Hom chain (affine-space adjunction N=ℓ over Noetherian V, closed adjoint, Yoneda in D+) and the Step 12 transpose. Two repairable faults, both fixed. (1) E2/E1: the new node asserted one uniform cohomological-dimension bound for all sheaves in the nonproper quasi-excellent case, copied from BS 6.7.1's wording.
